chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from one of our companions, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) did not speak to the servants with the full depth of his own intellect at all. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'We, the assembly of Prophets, have been commanded to speak to the people in accordance with their intellects.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet adapt his speech to the intellect of his audience?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *tawqi* (divine adaptation) in prophetic communication, noting that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) tailored his discourse to the intellectual capacity of his audience rather than conveying the absolute depth of divine truth. This hadith, found in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia understanding of the Prophet's wisdom in bridging the gap between infinite divine knowledge and finite human comprehension, a concept central to interpreting the layers of Quranic meaning.
